2892.h: 51 - al-Ashʿarī ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq *
2892.t:
The eminent scholar (العلامة), the Imam (الإمام) of the theologians (المتكلم), Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Bishr Isḥāq ibn Sālim ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā, son of the amir of Basra Bilāl ibn Abī Burdah, son of the companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ Abū Mūsā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays ibn Ḥaḍḍār al-Ashʿarī, al-Yamānī, al-Baṣrī.
He was born: in the year 260 AH, and it was said: rather he was born in the year 70. ⟦15:85⟧
He learned from: أبي خليفة الجمحي، وأبي علي الجبائي، وزكريا الساجي، وسهل بن نوح، وطبقتهم, and he narrates from them a great deal with a chain of transmission (الإسناد) in his exegesis (التفسير).
He was a marvel in intelligence and strength of understanding.
When he had become proficient in the knowledge of Iʿtizāl, he came to detest it and disowned it; he went up before the people and repented to Allah the Exalted from it, then he began to refute the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) and to expose their flaws.
The jurist (الفقيه) Abū Bakr al-Ṣayrafī said: the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) had raised their heads until al-Ashʿarī arose and confined them within sesame husks (1) .
From Ibn al-Bāqillānī, who said: the best of my states is that I understand the words of al-Ashʿarī (2) .
I say: I have seen four works by Abū al-Ḥasan on the fundamentals in which he sets out the principles of the school of the Salaf (السلف) on the attributes, and he said in them: they are passed on as they came.
Then he said: that is what I hold, by it I worship, and they are not to be interpreted figuratively.
I say: he died in Baghdad in the year 324 AH; a group of the Ḥanbalīs and of the scholars disparaged him (4) .
Everyone's words may be taken or left, except one whom Allah the Exalted has protected. O Allah, guide us and have mercy on us (5) . ⟦15:86⟧
Abū al-Ḥasan had an exceptional intelligence and vast erudition, and he has some good things, and numerous works that attest to the breadth of his knowledge.
Learning from him: Imams (الإمام), among them: أبو الحسن الباهلي (1) ، وأبو الحسن الكرماني، وأبو زيد المروزي، وأبو عبد الله بن مجاهد البصري، وبندار بن الحسين الشيرازي، وأبو محمد العراقي، وزاهر بن أحمد السرخسي، وأبو سهل الصعلوكي، وأبو نصر الكواز (2) الشيرازي (3) .
Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī said in his book (al-ʿUmad fī al-Ruʾyah): I compiled (al-Fuṣūl fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Mulḥidīn), which is twelve books; the book (al-Mūjaz) ; the book (Khalq al-Aʿmāl) ; the book (al-Ṣifāt) , which is large, in which we discussed the varieties of the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) and the Jahmiyyah (الجهمية); the book (al-Ruʾyah bi-al-Abṣār) ; the book (al-Khāṣṣ wa-al-ʿĀmm) ; the book (al-Radd ʿalā al-Mujassimah) ; the book (Īḍāḥ al-Burhān) ; the book (al-Lumaʿ fī al-Radd ʿalā Ahl al-Bidaʿ) ; the book (al-Sharḥ wa-al-Tafṣīl) ; the book (al-Naqḍ ʿalā al-Jubbāʾī (4)) ; the book (al-Naqḍ ʿalā al-Balkhī (5)) ; the book (Jumal Maqālāt al-Mulḥidīn) ; and a book (6) on the attributes, which is the largest of our books, in which we refuted what we had formerly composed on them in support of the school of the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة); ⟦15:87⟧ no book like it had been composed for them; then Allah made the truth clear to us and we retracted.
And a book in (al-Radd ʿalā Ibn al-Rāwandī) ; the book (al-Qāmiʿ fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Khālidī) ; the book (Adab al-Jadal) ; the book (Jawāb al-Khurāsāniyyah) ; the book (Jawāb al-Sīrāfiyyīn) ; and (Jawāb al-Jurjāniyyīn) ; the book (al-Masāʾil al-Manthūrah al-Baghdādiyyah) ; the book (al-Funūn fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Mulḥidīn) ; the book (al-Nawādir fī Daqāʾiq al-Kalām) and the book (Tafsīr al-Qurʾān) .
And he named many other books besides these.
Then after (al-ʿUmad) he compiled several books, which Ibn Fūrak named; they are in (Tabyīn Kadhib al-Muftarī (1)) .
I have seen a statement of al-Ashʿarī that pleased me, and it is firmly established; al-Bayhaqī narrated it: سمعت أبا حازم العبدوي، سمعت زاهر بن أحمد السرخسي يقول: when the appointed time of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī drew near in my house in Baghdad, he called me and I came to him, and he said: bear witness against me that I do not declare anyone of the people of the qiblah an unbeliever, because all of them point to one object of worship; all this is only a difference of expressions.
I say: and something like this is what I hold as my religion; likewise our shaykh Ibn Taymiyyah used to say in his last days: I do not declare anyone (2) of the Ummah an unbeliever; and he would say:
The Prophet ﷺ said: (None preserves his ablution except a believer (3)) ; so whoever keeps to the prayers with ablution is a Muslim. ⟦15:88⟧
Al-Ahwāzī (1) compiled a hadith fascicle (الجزء) on the faults of Ibn Abī Bishr, containing lies.
Abū al-Qāsim collected in his virtues useful notes, some of which are also not authentic (الصحيح). He had the well known (المشهور) debate with al-Jubbāʾī on their saying: it is obligatory upon Allah to do what is best; al-Ashʿarī said: rather, He does what He wills (2) ; what do you say about three children: one of them died, and two grew up, of whom one believed and the other disbelieved; what is the reason for cutting off the child?
He said: because Allah the Exalted knew that had he reached maturity he would have disbelieved, so cutting him off was best for him.
Al-Ashʿarī said: but He kept one of them alive and he disbelieved.
He said: He only kept him alive to expose him to the highest ranks.
Al-Ashʿarī said: then why did He not keep the child alive to expose him to the highest ranks?
Al-Jubbāʾī said: you have been seized by whisperings.
He said: no, by Allah, but the shaykh's donkey has stopped.
It has reached us that Abū al-Ḥasan repented, ascended the pulpit of Basra and said: I used to hold the creation of the Qurʾān (خلق القرآن), and that Allah is not seen with the eyes (3) , and that evil is my own act, not by decree; and I am repentant, holding to the refutation of the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) (4) .
There was in him playfulness and much jesting.
Ibn Khallikān (5) said this.
He wrote many books, and he was content with little; he had part of a village from the endowment (الوقف) of their ancestor ⟦15:89⟧ the amir Bilāl ibn Abī Burdah (1) .
It is said: he lived on until the year 330 AH.

4149.h: 73 - Ibn Bundār ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿIjlī *
4149.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the exemplar (القدوة), Shaykh al-Islām (شيخ الإسلام), Abū al-Faḍl ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, son of the hadith scholar (المحدث) Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Bundār al-ʿIjlī, al-Rāzī, Meccan by birth, the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ).
He recited to Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Mujāhidī, the student of Ibn Mujāhid; he recited the reading of Ibn ⟦18:135⟧ ʿĀmir to the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ) of Damascus, ʿAlī ibn Dāwūd al-Dārānī; and he recited in Baghdad to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ḥammāmī and a group.
He heard in Mecca from: أحمد بن فراس، وعلي بن جعفر السيرواني الزاهد، ووالده أبي العباس بن بندار، وبالري من جعفر بن فناكي.
And in Baghdad from: أبي الحسن الرفاء، وعدة.
And in Damascus from: عبد الوهاب الكلابي.
And in Isfahan from: أبي عبد الله بن مندة.
And in Basra, Kufa, Harran, Tustar, al-Ruhā, Fasā, Ḥimṣ, Egypt, al-Ramlah, Nishapur, Nasā and Jurjān; he roamed the horizons for most of his life, and he was one of the unique figures of the age in knowledge and practice.
Learning from him: المستغفري (1) أحد شيوخه، وأبو بكر الخطيب، وأبو صالح المؤذن، ونصر بن محمد الشيرازي؛ شيخ للسلفي، وأبو علي الحداد، ومحمد بن عبد الواحد الدقاق، والحسين بن عبد الملك الخلال، وأبو سهل بن سعدويه، وفاطمة بنت البغدادي، وخلق.
In Egypt he met Abū Muslim al-Kātib (2) .
ʿAbd al-Ghāfir ibn Ismāʿīl said: he was reliable (ثقة), much-travelled, an Imam (الإمام) in the recitation traditions (القراءات), unique in his way; the shaykhs used to venerate him; he would not reside in the Sufi lodges (الخانقاه), but would take shelter in a ruined mosque, and when his place became known he would move away; he would not take anything from anyone, and when something came his way he would give it away to others (3) .
Yaḥyā ibn Mandah said: a group recited the Qurʾān to him; he left us for ⟦18:136⟧ Kirmān, and narrated there.
He died in the town of Awshīr: in Jumādā al-Ūlā in the year 454 AH.
He said: he was born in the year 371 AH; he is reliable (ثقة), scrupulous, religious, knowledgeable in the recitation traditions (القراءات), learned in literature and grammar; he is too great for one like me to point him out, more famous than the sun and brighter than the moon, a master of many disciplines of knowledge; he was imposing, looked up to, eloquent, of good conduct, and of great weight (1) .
Al-Silafī said: I heard ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Salamah in Marand (2) say: Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī took al-Sīrawānī, the shaykh of the Sacred Precinct, as his model, and al-Sīrawānī kept the company of Abū Muḥammad al-Murtaʿish (3) , the companion of al-Junayd.
Al-Khallāl said: Abū al-Faḍl the Imam (الإمام) set out towards Kirmān, and the people escorted him; he sent them back and took to the road alone, saying:
When we travel by night and you are our leader ... the mention of you suffices our mounts as a camel-driver's song (4)
Al-Khallāl said: and he recited to me verses of his own:
O Death, how harsh you are as a visitor ... you descend upon a man against his will
You take the virgin from her chamber ... and you take the only child from his mother
Al-Samʿānī said in (al-Dhayl) : he was an excellent Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ), of many works, ⟦18:137⟧ of good conduct, an ascetic (الزاهد), devoted to worship, of rough living, solitary and content; he taught recitation and narrated hadith most of his time; he used to travel alone and enter the wildernesses (1) .
I read to Isḥāq al-Asadī: أخبرنا ابن خليل، أخبرنا خليل بن بدر، أخبرنا محمد بن عبد الواحد الدقاق قال:
There came to us the unique Imam (الإمام) Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī - may Allah grant him His good pleasure and settle him in His gardens - and he was an Imam (الإمام) among the reliable (ثقة) Imams (الإمام) in hadith, narrations, the Sunnah (السنة) and the verses; the mention of him fills the mouth and makes the eye shed tears. He came to Isfahan several times, and I heard a good portion from him; he was an imposing man, tall of stature, a friend of Allah among the friends of Allah, a possessor of saintly wonders; he travelled the world benefiting others and benefiting himself (2) .
Al-Khallāl said: Abū al-Faḍl was on a road, and with him were bread and fānīdh (3) , and highwaymen wanted to take it from him, but he drove them off with his staff; he was asked about that, and he said: because it was lawful, and I might not find the like of it (4) .
He entered Kirmān in shabby attire, wearing worn-out rags, and was brought to the king; they said: a spy.
The king said: what is the news?
He said: are you asking me about the news of the earth or the news of heaven? If you are asking me about the news of heaven, then “Every day He is engaged in some matter” [Qurʾān 55:29], and if you are asking me about the news of the earth, then “Everyone upon it will perish” [Qurʾān 55:26]. The king marvelled at his words, honoured him and offered him money, but he did not accept it (5) . ⟦18:138⟧

3117.h: 274 - al-Ṣibghī Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Ayyūb al-Naysābūrī *
3117.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the eminent scholar (العلامة), the mufti (المفتي), the hadith scholar (المحدث), Shaykh al-Islām (شيخ الإسلام), Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Ayyūb ibn Yazīd al-Naysābūrī, al-Shāfiʿī, known as: al-Ṣibghī (3) .
He was born: in the year 258 AH. ⟦15:483⟧
He saw Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad al-Dhuhlī and Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī.
He heard: الفضل بن محمد الشعراني، وإسماعيل بن قتيبة، ويوسف بن يعقوب القزويني، والحارث بن أبي أسامة، وهشام بن علي السيرافي، وعلي بن عبد العزيز البغوي، وإسماعيل القاضي، ومحمد بن أيوب البجلي وطبقتهم بنيسابور والحجاز والبصرة وبغداد والري.
He collected and compiled, excelled in jurisprudence (الفقه), and distinguished himself in the science of hadith.
He performed the Hajj in the year 283 AH, and Abū al-Qāsim al-Baghawī read for him before his uncle (Muntaqā al-Musnad) .
Narrating from him: حمزة بن محمد الزيدي، وأبو علي الحافظ، وأبو أحمد الحاكم، وأبو بكر الإسماعيلي، ومحمد بن إبراهيم الجرجاني، وأبو عبد الله الحاكم، وخلق كثير.
Al-Ḥākim said: I heard him say: when I grew up, I occupied myself with learning horsemanship and did not hear a single letter; I was taken to Rayy while Abū Ḥātim was alive, and I asked him about a question concerning the inheritance of my father; then we returned to Nishapur in the year 280 AH. While I was at the door of our house, with Abū Ḥāmid ibn al-Sharqī and Abū Ḥāmid ibn Ḥasnawayh sitting there, they said to me: occupy yourself with the direct hearing (السماع) of hadith.
I said: from whom?
They said: from Ismāʿīl ibn Qutaybah.
So I went to him and heard, and came to love hadith; then I set out for Iraq a year later.
Al-Ḥākim said: the Imam (الإمام) Abū Bakr remained issuing legal opinions in Nishapur for fifty-odd years, and not a single question in which he erred was held against him in his legal opinions (الفتوى) (1) .
He has the extensive books such as (al-Ṭahārah) , ⟦15:484⟧ (al-Ṣalāh) , (al-Zakāh) , and so on to the end of the book (al-Mabsūṭ) .
I heard Abū al-Faḍl ibn Ibrāhīm say:
Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq used to deputise for the Imam of Imams (الإمام) Ibn Khuzaymah in giving legal opinions (الفتوى) for ten-odd years, in the congregational mosque and elsewhere.
Then al-Ḥākim said: I heard the shaykh Abū Bakr say: I saw in my dream as though I were in a house in which ʿUmar was, and the people had gathered around him asking him questions, and he gestured to me to answer them; I kept on being asked and answering while he was saying to me:
You are right, go on; you are right, go on.
I said: O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين), what is the salvation from this world, or the way out of it?
He said to me with his finger: supplication. I repeated the question to him, and he drew himself together as though he were prostrating out of humility, then he said: supplication.
Al-Ḥākim said: among his works are the book (al-Asmāʾ wa-al-Ṣifāt) , the book (al-Īmān) , the book (al-Qadar) , the book (al-Khulafāʾ al-Arbaʿah) , the book (al-Ruʾyah) , the book (al-Aḥkām) - it was carried to Baghdad and the praise of it was abundant - meaning: this work -, and the book (al-Imāmah) .
I heard him addressing a middle-aged man from among the people of (1) ; he said: they narrated to us from Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb; and the man said to him: leave us alone with "he narrated to us"; how long will it be "he narrated to us" and "he informed us"?
He said: O you, I do not smell the scent of faith in your words, and it is not lawful for you to enter this house; then he shunned him until he died.
Al-Ḥākim said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Ḥamdūn say: I kept the company of Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq for years, and I never saw him abandon the night prayer, neither when travelling nor when at home (2) . ⟦15:485⟧
I saw Abū Bakr more than once after the call to prayer supplicating and weeping, and sometimes he would strike his head against the wall, until one day I feared that his head would bleed; I did not see among all our shaykhs anyone better in prayer than him, and he would not let anyone backbite in his gathering (1) .
I heard him more than once, when he recited a verse of poetry, spoil it and alter it until the metre was gone; and his intellect (2) and judgement were proverbial.
He was asked about someone who catches the bowing without having recited al-Fātiḥah, and he said: he repeats the rakʿah (3) .
Then al-Ḥākim said: حدثنا أبو بكر بن إسحاق، حدثنا يوسف بن يعقوب القزويني، حدثنا سعيد بن يحيى الأصبهاني، حدثنا سعير بن الخمس، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي الأحوص، عن عبد الله، قال:
Whoever would love to meet Allah tomorrow as a Muslim, let him guard these five prayers wherever the call is made for them.
Al-Ḥākim said: al-Dāraquṭnī wrote this from me, and said: I have never written it from anyone.
Al-Khalīlī narrated it from al-Ḥākim, and al-Khalīlī said: Ibn Mandah narrated it from al-Ṣibghī.
Ibn Mandah said: Abū al-Shaykh the hadith master (الحافظ) wrote it from me.
A group narrated it from al-Hajarī.
It has come from Suʿayr only by this route, from Abū Isḥāq, and he is Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī (4) , not al-Sabīʿī; then al-Khalīlī went to great lengths in extolling him. ⟦15:486⟧
Al-Ḥākim said: I heard Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq say:
We came out of the session of Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī, and with us was a very licentious man; he saw a beardless youth, went up to him and said:
Peace be upon you, and he shook his hand, kissed his eyes and his cheek, then said: al-Dabarī narrated to us in Ṣanʿāʾ with his chain of transmission (الإسناد), saying:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (If one of you loves his brother, let him inform him (1)) .
I said to him: are you not ashamed to commit sodomy and to lie in hadith?
Meaning: that he had fabricated a chain of transmission (الإسناد) for the text.
Al-Ṣibghī died in Shaʿbān in the year 342 AH.
In that year died: the musnid (المسند) of Hamadhān, Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn ʿUbayd al-Asadī; the shaykh of the Sufis (الصوفي), Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muwallad; the musnid (المسند) Abū al-Faḍl al-Ḥasan ibn Yaʿqūb al-Bukhārī; the musnid (المسند) ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥamdān al-Jallāb in Hamadhān; the judge (القاضي) and eminent scholar (العلامة) Abū al-Qāsim ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Fahm al-Tanūkhī; the shaykh of Marw, the Imam (الإمام) Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qāsim ibn al-Qāsim ibn Mahdī al-Sayyārī, grandson of Aḥmad ibn Sayyār ⟦15:487⟧ the hadith master (الحافظ); the musnid (المسند) Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Aswārī al-Aṣbahānī; and the shaykh of the hadith scholars (المحدث) and the ascetics (الزاهد) in Nishapur, Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūrī.
I read to Abū al-Maʿālī Aḥmad ibn al-Muʾayyad: أخبرنا محمد بن محمد المأموني، أخبرنا أحمد بن محمد الحافظ، أخبرنا القاسم بن الفضل، حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن جعفر اليزدي إملاء، أخبرنا أبو بكر أحمد بن إسحاق بن أيوب الصبغي، حدثنا محمد بن غالب بن حرب، حدثنا داود بن عبد الله الجعفري، حدثنا مالك عن نافع:
From Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands when he said the takbīr and when he rose (1) .
And by the same chain: أخبرنا الصبغي، حدثنا أحمد بن القاسم بن أبي مساور، حدثنا أبو معمر إسماعيل بن إبراهيم قال:
Ibn Wahb dictated to me from his memory, عن يونس، عن الزهري:
From Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: (There is no amputation for one who plunders, nor for one who snatches, nor for one who betrays a trust) (2) . ⟦15:488⟧
Very gharīb (الغريب).
Despite the uprightness of its narrators, narration of it should only be from a book, for I consider that Ibn Wahb, despite his memory, erred in it; and the text has a chain of transmission (الإسناد) other than this.
His brother:

5582.h: 156 - Ibn Baqī Aḥmad ibn Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Umawī *
5582.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the eminent scholar (العلامة), the hadith scholar (المحدث), the musnid (المسند), the judge (القاضي) of the community, Abū al-Qāsim Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Walīd Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Makhlad ibn ʿAbd ⟦22:274⟧ al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad, son of the shaykh of Andalusia, the hadith master (الحافظ) Baqī ibn Makhlad, al-Umawī, their client (المولى), al-Baqawī, al-Qurṭubī, al-Mālikī.
He heard: أباه، وجده؛ أبا الحسن، ومحمد بن عبد الحق الخزرجي صاحب محمد بن الفرج الطلاعي، وخلف بن بشكوال، وأبا زيد السهيلي (1) ، وطائفة.
He was granted a licence to transmit (الإجازة) by: المقرئ أبو الحسن شريح بن محمد، وعبد الملك بن مسرة.
He was alone in transmitting certain things, among them (the Muwaṭṭaʾ of Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā) , from al-Khazrajī.
He narrated hadith, he and all his forefathers.
Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Abbār (2) said: he is one of the great men of Andalusia in eminence and perfection; we know of no house more deeply rooted than his in knowledge and distinction except the house of the Banū Mughīth in Cordoba and that of the Banū al-Bājī in Seville, and he has precedence over them. He was appointed chief judge in Marrakesh, in addition to the two offices of the court of grievances and the supreme chancery; his conduct was praised, and elevation only increased him in humility. Then he was dismissed and remained without office (3) until he was entrusted with the judgeship of his own city, and he went there; then he was dismissed before his death, and the students thronged to him, and he was worthy of that.
Ibn al-Zubayr - or someone else - said: he had a long reach in grammar and literature; people competed in learning from him; he read the whole of (the Book of Sībawayh) with Abū al-ʿAbbās ibn Maḍāʾ, and he read (al-Maqāmāt) with him.
Ibn Musdī said: this shaykh of ours attained leadership in both Maghribs, and held the judgeship on both shores; when he grew old he asked to be relieved and returned to his city, where he remained as judge (القاضي) until ⟦22:275⟧ old age overcame him, and he kept to his house. He was knowledgeable in consensus (الإجماع) and juristic disagreement (الخلاف), inclined to weighing the evidence and to fairness.
I say: Narrating from him: المعمر أبو محمد بن هارون الذي كتب إلينا بالإجازة من المغرب، وجماعة.
Narrating from him by licence to transmit (الإجازة): محمد بن عياش الخزرجي، والخطيب أبو القاسم بن الأيسر الجذامي، وأبو الحكم مالك بن المرحل الأديب، وآخرون.
He (may Allah have mercy on him) was dominated by an inclination to the school of the people of transmitted reports and of the literal sense in his affairs and his rulings.
Among those who narrated from him: العلامة أبو الحسين بن أبي الربيع، and by licence to transmit (الإجازة): محمد بن محمد المومنائي الفاسي.
أخبرنا عبد الله بن محمد بن هارون الطائي الفقيه إذنا، قال: أنبأنا أحمد بن يزيد القاضي، عن شريح بن محمد المقرئ، عن الفقيه أبي محمد بن حزم، أخبرنا يحيى بن عبد الرحمن، أخبرنا قاسم بن أصبغ، حدثنا إبراهيم بن عبد الله العبسي، حدثنا وكيع، عن الأعمش، عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Fasting is a shield (1)) .
Ibn Baqī was born: in the year 537 AH.
He died: on Friday, after the prayer, in mid-Ramaḍān of the year 625 AH, in Cordoba, having passed 88 years of age (may Allah have mercy on him); he was the last ⟦22:276⟧ to narrate (the Muwaṭṭaʾ) in the world with an elevated chain (العالي): between him and the Imam (الإمام) Mālik in it are six men with continuous direct hearing (السماع). The same number holds in (the Muwaṭṭaʾ) of Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr for Mukarram ibn Abī al-Ṣaqr al-Bazzāz; in (the Muwaṭṭaʾ of al-Qaʿnabī) for the two Muwaffaqs, Ibn Qudāmah and ʿAbd al-Laṭīf, and for Ibn al-Khayr; in (the Muwaṭṭaʾ of Abū Muṣʿab) for Abū Naṣr ibn al-Shīrāzī and Ibn al-Burhān; and in (the Muwaṭṭaʾ of Suwayd ibn Saʿīd) for al-Bahāʾ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
